title: Requests and commands
description: Ask people to do things politely, tell friends and children what to do, and say 'don't'.

guide.title: Familiar and polite commands
guide.text:
The bare verb stem is the command to someone you call neenu - a child, a close friend: maadu (do!), hogu (go!), nodu (look!), kodu (give!).

For everyone else, and for more than one person, replace the final -u with -i. This form is already polite and needs no 'please': ಮಾಡಿ (maadi), ಹೋಗಿ (hogi), ನೋಡಿ (nodi), ಕೇಳಿ (keli), ಕೊಡಿ (kodi), ಹೇಳಿ (heli), ಇರಿ (iri).

Two very common verbs are irregular:
baa (come) - ಬನ್ನಿ (banni).
taa (bring) - ತನ್ನಿ (tanni).
(tinnu, 'eat', is regular - ತಿನ್ನಿ (tinni) - and only looks like them.)

Verbs ending in -i or -e add -yiri: kudi (drink) - ಕುಡಿಯಿರಿ (kudiyiri); kare (call) - ಕರೆಯಿರಿ (kareyiri); bare (write) - ಬರೆಯಿರಿ (bareyiri); tere (open) - ತೆರೆಯಿರಿ (tereyiri). In speech these are shortened: kudeeri, kareeri.

Verbs ending in -ko (the short spoken form of -kollu) take -kolli: kootko (sit) - ಕೂತ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ (kootkolli); tago (take) - ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ (tagolli).

guide.title: Softening a request
guide.text:
The -i form is polite, but a bare command can still sound abrupt. Kannada speakers soften requests in several ways:

ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ (svalpa) 'a little' before the verb: svalpa iri, 'wait a bit, please'; svalpa nodi, 'have a look, would you'.

An address word: saar, medam, anna, akka.

A question instead of a command: svalpa sahaaya maadteeraa? 'will you help a little?'; ee kelasa maadoke aaguttaa? 'would it be possible to do this?'

ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು (dayavittu) 'please' is for formal situations and written notices.

Adverbs of manner go before the verb: ಬೇಗ (bega) quickly; ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ (nidhaanavaagi) slowly; ಜೋರಾಗಿ (joraagi) loudly, fast; ಮೆಲ್ಲಗೆ (mellage) softly, gently.

guide.title: Don't, and 'let him'
guide.text:
Negative command: verb stem + -a + ಬೇಡ (beda) for neenu, + ಬೇಡಿ (bedi) for neevu. maadabeda / maadabedi (don't do), hogabedi (don't go), mareyabedi (don't forget), helabedi (don't tell). Verbs in -i and -e insert y: mare - mareyabedi; kudi - kudiyabedi.

'Let him / her / it / them ...' is the stem + -ಅಲಿ (-ali): ಬರಲಿ (barali) let him come; ಇರಲಿ (irali) let it be - a very common word meaning 'never mind, leave it'; ಆಗಲಿ (aagali) let it be so - a polite 'very well'.

For 'let's' use -ona (hogona) and for 'shall I' use -alaa (baralaa?), as in the unit on the future.
